todays_goal: Turn TacticLab into a visual coaching tool with animated tactical movement and a replayable corner routine.

lessons.subject: computer_science
lessons.unit_title: Creative Technology and AI Builder Lab
lessons.previous_learning: Day 20 core coaching controls were functionally tested: width, defensive line, attack style, pressing, save, and reset.
lessons.course_context: Earn the creative upgrade by adding animated tactic playback and a corner routine.
learning_objectives: Keep animation compatible with formation state.
Design and test a purposeful corner routine.
Document one bug with a behavioral test report.
lessons.why_it_matters: Animation turns static tactics into an understandable simulation and introduces sequencing, timing, state transitions, and replayability.

vocabulary.definition: an ordered sequence showing when movements happen
whether an animation is playing, paused, stopped, or reset
a saved arrangement or behavior that can be loaded quickly

lessons.written_instruction: Laptop only. Add smooth tactic playback, then build one replayable corner routine with at least three purposeful movements.

worked_examples.title: Movement timeline
worked_examples.problem: How do three runners move without chaos?
worked_examples.solution: Place each movement on a 0-4 second timeline and define start/end positions.
worked_examples.explanation: Timing makes the tactic understandable and testable.

guided_practice.prompt: Whiteboard a 0-4 second movement timeline and START -> PLAY -> MOVE -> END -> RESET state flow.

independent_practice.prompt: Verify formation switching does not break playback.
Build a corner routine with near-post, far-post, and edge/short-option movements.
Replay the corner routine multiple times.
Document and fix one bug using EXPECTED / ACTUAL / STEPS / RETEST.

exit_ticket.prompt: Demo the animation and corner routine. Explain how reset and formation state are preserved.
exit_ticket.answer: Live demonstration of functional playback, reset, and replay.

lessons.voice_prompt: Laptop only. Use the whiteboard for a timeline and state flow. Keep questions product-focused: what should move, when, and where? Do not teach syntax unless asked. Require functional testing of play, reset, formation compatibility, and replay.
lessons.teacher_notes: Creative upgrade earned after Day 20 functional pass.
